📄 Paper Board.what: Coordinates one paper: its ideas, evidence, versions and submission outputs.
📄 Paper Board.layout: Report → Review Content → Around the Work
📄 Paper Board.example: One Board reuses its evidence across two writing versions.

🧭 Around the Work.what: The eight shared sections use the current View’s scope; the right rail aggregates the Board and descendants.
🧭 Around the Work.layout: Unnumbered sections in the shared order
🧭 Around the Work.example: An unassigned review question remains in the right rail until a View or Topic is linked.

🔀 Directions.what: Compare candidate research directions and the recorded selection.
🔀 Directions.example: Compare candidate questions, theory and evidence needs; keep the recorded verdict beside each direction.

🎓 Theory.what: Read the theoretical basis of the candidate direction or chosen Story.
🎓 Theory.layout: Idea: Left Tabs · Right Content; Story: Paragraph
🎓 Theory.example: State which theory is tested or extended and what the proposed result would add.

📌 Open points.what: Read unresolved points recorded by the current Topic.
📌 Open points.example: A Story question is still waiting for a choice of scope.

🧭 Direction.what: Read the direction chosen for the paper.
🧭 Direction.example: The selected policy, outcome and population define the telling.

💡 Pitch.what: Read what the paper claims and why the question matters.
💡 Pitch.example: A short pitch connects the question, contribution and intended reader.

❓ Research Questions.what: Read each research question with its narrative and recorded state.
❓ Research Questions.example: RQ0 describes the cohort; RQ1 asks about the main effect; RQ2 asks for whom it changes.

⚖️ Stakes and evidence.what: Compare why an answer matters with the evidence and boundaries supporting it.
⚖️ Stakes and evidence.example: Keep the claimed contribution within the study design’s supported scope.

📚 Related.what: Read related papers under the question each paper bears on.
📚 Related.example: A prior study can support more than one question without duplicating its source record.

🏛️ Venues.what: Review target venues, fit and remaining desk requirements.
🏛️ Venues.example: Read the venue’s call and identify the contribution to lead with.

🧠 Story by Section.what: See where the claims land in the manuscript’s reader order.
🧠 Story by Section.example: C1 appears in Introduction and Results; C2 appears in Results and Discussion.

🗄️ Data flow.what: Follow how the inputs become the evidence needed for each question.
🗄️ Data flow.example: Cohort → outcomes and covariates → estimates → evidence for RQ1.

📝 Paper flow.what: Follow the manuscript’s section order and the route to a send.
📝 Paper flow.example: Question → Methods → Results → Discussion → assembled manuscript.

🗺️ Roadmaps.what: Read the planned discovery and internal analysis work.
🗺️ Roadmaps.example: A roadmap row names the work, its source location, state and the question it feeds.

🧭 Plan.what: Open the planning work and copy the prompt for the responsible skill.
🧭 Plan.example: Design the dataset, analysis, execution, displays and reading. Copying a prompt does not execute it.

⚙️ Runs to do.what: Inspect the work and Runs named in the Story’s Task roadmap.
⚙️ Runs to do.example: Open the referenced Task or Run to inspect its actual execution record.

🗓️ Next steps to the send.what: Read recorded steps and dates leading to the manuscript send.
🗓️ Next steps to the send.example: Finish a missing Section, rebuild and check the submission materials.

🧪 Work.what: Browse internal analysis Blocks referenced by the paper.
🧪 Work.example: Expand a supporting Block through its Jobs and Tasks to the actual Runs.

🔎 Discovery.what: Browse referenced literature Blocks and their reading Runs.
🔎 Discovery.example: Open the reading Run behind a cited source while retaining the tree position.

🔢 Values.what: The values renderer presents a group of values or a whole-paper audit result.
🔢 Values.layout: Left value tabs · Right result and checks
🔢 Values.example: The parent evidence Job and returned values.yaml select this presentation. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

📚 Citations.what: Citation records and verification; at Task level the same renderer serves claim groups and whole-paper audits.
📚 Citations.layout: Left citation tabs · Right source/check records
📚 Citations.example: Use Cases selects a claim group or the whole-paper audit. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

📐 Plan.what: Read the display plan and its venue constraints.
📐 Plan.example: Plan the main figure and supplement with the permitted display count and format.

🖼️ Displays.what: Inspect the rendered figures and tables.
🖼️ Displays.layout: Left Tabs · Right Content → PDF preview
🖼️ Displays.example: Choose a main or supplementary display and read its current preview.

🔍 Examples.what: Inspect reference displays collected for the target venue.
🔍 Examples.example: Compare layout and presentation choices against published examples.

✍️ Version sections.what: Read Sections within each writing version; the actual section heading is the version name.
✍️ Version sections.layout: Left Tabs · Right Content → Draft section
✍️ Version sections.example: Select Introduction or Methods within the first or revised writing version.

📄 The assembled paper.what: Read a version’s existing built manuscript. This section appears when an output is present.
📄 The assembled paper.example: Inspect the assembled PDF and Word output together with their build state.

📮 Ready for the portal.what: Inspect the existing submission outputs for a version.
📮 Ready for the portal.example: Read the cover letter and portal materials; their presence alone is not submission approval.

🪜 Sections to finish.what: Open each manuscript Section’s recorded draft steps.
🪜 Sections to finish.example: Find the Section that needs evidence review or writing before the next build.

🎨 Studio.what: AI and people develop and compare design options from findings and feedback.

🙋 Interactions.what: Questions and feedback for the selected topic.
🙋 Interactions.outcome: Answers linked to their original topic.
🙋 Interactions.layout_detail: Topics on the left; questions and their form on the right.

⚖️ Decisions.layout_detail: Topics on the left; source decision records on the right.

📚 Things to Know.what: Find the terms, assumptions, and references needed here.

📝 Checklist.what: Read the checks recorded for this View or Topic. Completion is taken from the source record.
📝 Checklist.example: A display review or evidence check remains open until its source is updated.

🕒 Timeline.what: Read dated Runs, feedback and decisions linked to this View; the right rail gathers the Board’s history.

🧰 Skills.what: Find the skills that help maintain this view.
🧰 Skills.layout: Left Tabs · Right Content → Skill Details

📁 Files.what: Related directories grouped by Workspace, Blocks, Code, Tools · Skills and Tools · UI.
📁 Files.outcome: Open, preview or download the original file.
📁 Files.layout: Left Folder Types · Right Folder Tree
📁 Files.layout_detail: Select a type, expand folders in the tree, and click a file to inspect it in a pop-out. Closing it keeps your place in the tree; Runs stay inside Blocks.

🧠 Version map.what: The version’s venue, Story and Sections, with previous-version and reviewer-response context when those records exist.
🧠 Version map.example: Source: version face and Section Tasks. Skill: haipipe-paper-draft.

🧠 Revision map.what: Earlier version, reviewer points, linked replies and revised Sections.
🧠 Revision map.example: Source: the version’s from: link and responds-to/report records. Skill: haipipe-paper-comments.

🧠 Task map.what: The Job’s Tasks, each purpose, result state and page link.
🧠 Task map.example: Source: Job face and child Tasks. Open a Task to inspect its actual record.

📝 Main text.what: The version’s main Sections in reader order.
📝 Main text.example: Source: t00–t19 draft Tasks. Work adds each Section’s next draft step. Skill: haipipe-paper-draft.

📝 Appendix and letters.what: The version’s appendix and letter Tasks.
📝 Appendix and letters.example: Current grouping includes t20–t39, including cover and response letters. Work adds draft-step actions.

🔎 Check.what: The evidence check’s actual findings and unresolved mismatches.
🔎 Check.example: Source: t99 check Task Results. Work adds the check’s Run and applicable binding proposals. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

✉️ Cover letter.what: The referenced writing Task’s letter, with its current draft state.
✉️ Cover letter.example: Source: submission for / words-in links. Work opens the letter’s next draft step. Skill: haipipe-paper-draft.

📮 Portal fields.what: Portal steps, required values, uploads and differences still to resolve.
📮 Portal fields.example: Source: portal-fields.yaml, submission values and existing outputs. Skill: haipipe-paper. Viewing does not submit.

🧠 Task purpose and Runs.what: The Task’s purpose, returned output and recorded Runs.
🧠 Task purpose and Runs.example: Source: Task face and Run records. A completed Run does not imply accepted output.

📝 The text.what: The latest draft or adopted text, with sentence evidence and change cards when present.
📝 The text.layout: Text on the left · Evidence and review cards on the right
📝 The text.example: Source: draft history and adopted Content. Review decisions are made in Work → Revise. Skill: haipipe-draft-writing.

💬 Points and replies.what: Each reviewer point beside its response and affected manuscript Sections.
💬 Points and replies.example: Source: responds-to links and the response draft. Skill: haipipe-paper-comments.

📋 Draft progress.what: The Task’s aim, current step and each draft step’s recorded state.
📋 Draft progress.example: Source: draft workflow records. Skills: haipipe-draft-workflow, haipipe-paper-draft.

📌 Headline.what: What the latest Run returned, with original result links.
📌 Headline.example: Source: Run Results and runtime records; starter portal data stays marked as a starter.

🧪 Runs.what: Recorded Runs, their purpose and execution state.
🧪 Runs.example: Source: runs/ and Result receipts. Skill: haipipe-run.

🖼️ Its display.what: The Task’s figure or table, input table and build details.
🖼️ Its display.layout: Left tabs · Right preview and source
🖼️ Its display.example: Source: display Run Results. Skill: haipipe-display.

🔢 Its values.what: Each value, its provenance and check result.
🔢 Its values.example: Source: values.yaml and returned tables. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

🔢 The raw tables.what: Returned source tables used for value selection.
🔢 The raw tables.example: Source: tables.json from the value build Run. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

📚 Its citations.what: Each citation key, source evidence and check status.
📚 Its citations.example: Source: citations.csv and source records. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

📋 Its facts.what: The Task’s recorded label, caption, question, source and completion conditions.
📋 Its facts.example: Source: Task face; only authored fields appear.

✉️ The letter.what: The letter text owned by the linked writing Task.
✉️ The letter.example: Source: words-in. Editing belongs to the writing Task’s draft workflow.

📮 The portal’s fields.what: The recorded portal steps and field definitions.
📮 The portal’s fields.layout: Left step tabs · Right field records
📮 The portal’s fields.example: Source: portal-fields.yaml. An unopened starter remains visibly unwalked.

📮 The fill page.what: The prepared submission fill page and its field values.
📮 The fill page.example: Source: existing portal-fill.html. Human review and submission remain separate.

📌 Step state.what: The current step’s state and any required human action.
📌 Step state.example: Source: draft workflow state. Displayed when there is a waiting or actionable state.

📥 Input.what: The actual inputs read by this writing step.
📥 Input.example: Source: the draft step’s input contract. Response planning also reads reviewer comments.

🏃 Step Runs.what: Runs attached to the selected writing step.
🏃 Step Runs.example: Source: writing Run records; shown when present.

📝 Plan and scratch.what: The Task’s structure, outline and notes.
📝 Plan and scratch.layout: Plan cards · Scratch editor when present
📝 Plan and scratch.example: Source: current draft plan. Skill: haipipe-draft-logic. Human plan approval remains explicit.

✍️ Draft text.what: The draft produced for this Section, summary or letter.
✍️ Draft text.example: Source: writing Results or adopted Content. Skill: haipipe-draft-writing.

🔎 Evidence and bib.what: Evidence requests, source bindings and the Section’s bibliography.
🔎 Evidence and bib.example: Source: the Task’s evidence records and bib. Skill: haipipe-evidence.

🖼️ Display review.what: The displays called for by this Task and their acceptance records.
🖼️ Display review.example: Conditional view: appears only when this Task calls for or has displays. Skill: haipipe-display.

💬 Review and revision.what: Review cards, proposed changes and recorded accept/reject decisions.
💬 Review and revision.example: Source: revision history. Skill: haipipe-draft-review. Human decisions are preserved.

🤖 Ask the agent.what: The existing prompts for the current writing step.
🤖 Ask the agent.example: Appears for Plan, Write and Revise when a prompt exists. Copying does not start a Run.

✍️ Writing Version.what: One manuscript version for a venue or send; its own Sections reuse Board evidence.
✍️ Writing Version.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🔁 Revised Version.what: A writing version linked to an earlier send, reviewer points and a response letter. It uses the writing-version renderer.
🔁 Revised Version.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🖼️ Display Evidence.what: The Board’s figure and table collection, its plan and venue examples.
🖼️ Display Evidence.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🔢 Value Evidence.what: The Board’s printed-value groups, source tables and whole-paper value check.
🔢 Value Evidence.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📚 Citation Evidence.what: The Board’s claim groups and whole-paper citation check.
📚 Citation Evidence.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📮 Submission.what: The materials and portal preparation for one named writing version.
📮 Submission.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📝 Manuscript Section.what: One main-text or appendix Section, with its own writing history and evidence.
📝 Manuscript Section.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📄 Abstract / Summary.what: A summary Task using the same draft workflow, with scope and constraints in its plan.
📄 Abstract / Summary.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

✉️ Cover Letter.what: The writing version’s cover-letter draft; submission references these words.
✉️ Cover Letter.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

💬 Reviewer Response.what: A response-letter draft with reviewer points linked to replies and affected Sections.
💬 Reviewer Response.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🖼️ Figure / Table.what: One display output with its preview, source table, build details and Runs.
🖼️ Figure / Table.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🔢 Value Group.what: One group of printed values traced to returned source results.
🔢 Value Group.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🗄️ Raw Value Tables.what: Source tables used to inspect and select values for the manuscript.
🗄️ Raw Value Tables.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🔎 Value Check.what: A whole-paper check Task comparing printed values with their source results.
🔎 Value Check.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📚 Citation Group.what: A claim group’s citation keys, source records and checks.
📚 Citation Group.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🔍 Citation Check.what: A whole-paper check Task for keys, citation cards and bibliography records.
🔍 Citation Check.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

✉️ Submission Letter.what: A submission Task referencing the writing version’s cover letter through words-in.
✉️ Submission Letter.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

🚶 Portal Walk.what: A recorded survey of the portal’s steps and fields; a starter is not a completed walk.
🚶 Portal Walk.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📮 Portal Fill.what: A prepared fill page for one submission. The person checks the fields and submits.
📮 Portal Fill.layout: One row per type; select its view to inspect its sections.

📝 Draft Task.what: One draft workflow for a Section, abstract, cover letter or reviewer response. The face declares task-type: draft; responds-to adds point/reply content.
📝 Draft Task.layout: Report reading views · Work writing steps
📝 Draft Task.example: Open a Use Case for a purpose-specific example. Skills: haipipe-draft-workflow, haipipe-paper-draft.

🖼️ Display Task.what: The display renderer presents a figure or table and its source/build records.
🖼️ Display Task.example: Figure and table preparation are uses of the same display branch. Skill: haipipe-display.

🗄️ Value Tables.what: The tables branch presents raw returned tables. It is selected by tables.json when values.yaml is absent, not by a new execution-type enum.
🗄️ Value Tables.layout: Left table tabs · Right source table
🗄️ Value Tables.example: Open Source table inspection. Skill: haipipe-paper-evidence.

💰 Grant Board.what: A type within the Paper theme for a grant application. It shares the Paper planning, evidence, writing-version, review and assembly structure, with funding-call, aims, team and budget requirements. Grant-specific behavior and examples are not implemented yet.
💰 Grant Board.layout: Report → Review Content → Around the Work
💰 Grant Board.example: An initial application and its resubmission share evidence and the research plan; each submission retains its own requirements.

🏛️ Funding call.what: Read the selected funding opportunity and its source documents.
🏛️ Funding call.example: A call defines the proposed scope and application documents.

✅ Eligibility and fit.what: Compare the proposal and team against the selected call’s stated eligibility and scope.
✅ Eligibility and fit.layout: Requirement rows with source and recorded assessment
✅ Eligibility and fit.example: A requirement remains unresolved until its supporting information is recorded.

📋 Application requirements.what: Track the exact documents, limits and evaluation criteria from the selected call.
📋 Application requirements.example: Each application document points to its required format and source.

🗓️ Deadlines.what: Show recorded sponsor and internal deadlines with their sources.
🗓️ Deadlines.example: Internal review precedes the recorded submission deadline.

❓ Research gap.what: State the unresolved problem the proposed research addresses.
❓ Research gap.example: The proposal identifies an unanswered question and the evidence for that gap.

🎯 Specific aims.what: State the proposed aims, expected outcomes and their dependencies.
🎯 Specific aims.example: Each aim links to its approach and measurable outcome.

✨ Significance and innovation.what: Explain why the proposed work matters and what it contributes.
✨ Significance and innovation.example: A contribution is supported by the documented research gap.

🔬 Approach.what: Describe how each aim will be investigated.
🔬 Approach.example: The method names inputs, analysis and success criteria.

🗓️ Milestones.what: Connect the proposed work to dated milestones and deliverables.
🗓️ Milestones.example: Each milestone names its output and responsible role.

⚠️ Risks and alternatives.what: Record feasibility risks and alternative approaches.
⚠️ Risks and alternatives.example: A dependency has a fallback if the planned input is unavailable.

👥 Team roles.what: Describe who contributes which capability and responsibility.
👥 Team roles.example: Each aim has an accountable role and required expertise.

💰 Budget and justification.what: Link proposed resources and their justification to the research plan.
💰 Budget and justification.example: A resource request identifies the work it supports; funder-specific rules come from the call.

🤝 Commitments.what: Track required support letters and institutional commitments.
🤝 Commitments.example: A requested letter has an owner and a received version.

🧪 Preliminary evidence.what: Present existing results that support feasibility, separate from proposed future outcomes.
🧪 Preliminary evidence.layout: Evidence tabs linked to source results
🧪 Preliminary evidence.example: A feasibility result points to the Work Block that produced it.

📚 Supporting literature.what: Connect proposal claims to verified literature.
📚 Supporting literature.example: A significance claim links to its supporting sources.

🖼️ Proposal figures.what: Read figures explaining the aims, approach and preliminary evidence.
🖼️ Proposal figures.example: A study schematic links each aim to its method.

📝 Proposal sections.what: Read the sections of one application version.
📝 Proposal sections.example: An aims page and research strategy belong to the same application version.

📄 Assembled proposal.what: Read the application documents assembled for a specific call.
📄 Assembled proposal.example: The preview contains the selected version’s required sections.

💬 Reviewer feedback.what: Link received feedback to the revisions that address it.
💬 Reviewer feedback.example: A resubmission links each response to a revised section.

📦 Application package.what: List the exact documents prepared for one submission.
📦 Application package.example: Each requested slot links to its prepared document.

✅ Readiness checks.what: Compare the prepared package against recorded call requirements and unresolved decisions.
✅ Readiness checks.example: An absent attachment remains unresolved; a built package is not evidence of submission.

📮 Submission record.what: Record the actual send and receipt when they exist.
📮 Submission record.example: Preparing the package does not mark it submitted.

Idea: haipipe-paper-related — Position candidate directions against related work.
Data + Paper Plan: haipipe-paper-plan — Maintain the data and paper plans.
Displays: haipipe-paper-story — Maintain the shared Story by Section.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

🖼️ Displays.what: Figures or tables read from the Board’s display Job, restricted to this view’s main/appendix placement when applicable.
🖼️ Displays.example: Source: display plan and original display Task Results. Work adds the linked display progress; viewing never copies evidence into this version.

📝 The text.what: The newest draft or adopted text; responds-to selects point/reply content for a reviewer-response Task.
📝 The text.example: Use Cases → Reviewer response opens that variant; all draft purposes keep the same Plan, Write, Evidence, Display and Revise workflow.

🧪 Work.what: Link internal Work Blocks that produce feasibility evidence or develop the proposed methods.
🧪 Work.example: Preliminary results retain their source Work Block.

🔎 Discovery.what: Link Discovery Blocks that establish the research gap and supporting literature.
🔎 Discovery.example: Verified literature informs the proposed aims.

🔀 Directions.what: Compare candidate grant directions against the research gap, feasibility and funding opportunity.
🔀 Directions.example: Two candidate directions are compared before selecting the application’s scope.

🎓 Theory.what: Explain the theoretical or conceptual basis for the proposed research and its aims.
🎓 Theory.example: A conceptual model connects the research gap to the expected mechanisms and outcomes.

📌 Open points.what: Track unresolved choices in the grant’s direction, narrative or preparation plan.
📌 Open points.example: A choice of study scope remains open until the team records a decision.

🧭 Direction.what: Read the selected direction and central argument of the grant proposal.
🧭 Direction.example: The chosen direction connects the problem, proposed approach and intended impact.

💡 Pitch.what: State the grant’s problem, proposed contribution and reason to fund it.
💡 Pitch.example: A short pitch explains why this work matters and why the approach is promising.

❓ Research Questions.what: Connect the proposed research questions and hypotheses to the specific aims.
❓ Research Questions.example: Each aim names a question and the evidence needed to answer it.

⚖️ Stakes and evidence.what: Connect the importance of the proposed work to existing evidence, uncertainty and feasibility.
⚖️ Stakes and evidence.example: Preliminary evidence supports feasibility without presenting proposed outcomes as established results.

📚 Related.what: Position the proposed research against related literature and existing approaches.
📚 Related.example: The narrative identifies what is already known and the gap the grant would address.

🏛️ Venues.what: For a grant, the target is the funding program or call. Read its fit and requirements from Opportunity.
🏛️ Venues.example: The narrative links to the selected call’s recorded evaluation criteria.
🏛️ Venues.layout: Left Tabs · Right Content → Funding call

🧠 Story by Section.what: Map the grant’s argument across its application sections.
🧠 Story by Section.example: Specific aims, significance, innovation and approach each carry part of one argument.

🗄️ Data flow.what: Map the data, access, preparation and analysis needed for the proposed aims; distinguish existing evidence from planned work.
🗄️ Data flow.example: Existing data supports a feasibility result; planned collection feeds a later aim.

📝 Paper flow.what: For a grant, map how the application sections use aims, evidence and figures to build the proposal.
📝 Paper flow.example: The aims page sets up the approach, supported by preliminary results and a study diagram.

🗺️ Roadmaps.what: Connect application preparation to the proposed research roadmap.
🗺️ Roadmaps.example: The preparation roadmap ends at submission; the research roadmap continues through the proposed milestones.

🧭 Plan.what: Plan the evidence, drafting and review work needed to prepare the grant application.
🧭 Plan.example: A missing feasibility result is linked to a Work Block; a drafting task uses its returned evidence.

⚙️ Runs to do.what: List the concrete Runs needed for application preparation and link them to their owning work.
⚙️ Runs to do.example: A literature check, feasibility analysis and section revision each have an assigned Run.

🗓️ Next steps to the send.what: Track the remaining preparation, review and package steps before the grant submission.
🗓️ Next steps to the send.example: The next steps complete the narrative, verify attachments and obtain the required human review.
